extracted.intended_audience: readers of philosophy and literary criticism (students, scholars, educated public interested in metaphysics and poetic theory)
extracted.subtask_description: Constructing and evaluating philosophical arguments about imagination, self-consciousness, and metaphysical method, and the appropriate style and terminology for such exposition. Applies to chapters or essays that bridge metaphysics and poetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth is correlative to being
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge without a correspondent reality is no knowledge; if we know, there must be somewhat known by us. To know is in its very essence a verb active.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a fundamental criterion for claims: a purported truth must correlate with being. Reject claims that posit knowledge divorced from any correspondent reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish immediate (absolute) and mediate (dependent) truths
rubrics_metrics.description: All truth is either mediate (derived from some other truth or truths) or immediate and original. The latter is absolute (formula A. A.); the former is of dependent or conditional certainty (formula B. A.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating certainty, identify whether a claim is self-grounded or derived. Beware of treating mediate truths as if they were absolute; trace chains of dependence to their first principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek a self-grounded absolute principle for knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: We are to seek some absolute truth capable of communicating to other positions a certainty which it has not itself borrowed; a truth self-grounded, unconditional and known by its own light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical systems should identify an ultimate principle that does not presuppose a further ground. Evaluate theories by whether they provide or presuppose such a self-evident foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle cannot be a mere thing or object
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a principle cannot be any THING or OBJECT. Each thing is what it is in consequence of some other thing; an infinite, independent thing is a contradiction. An object is inconceivable without a subject as its antithesis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid locating the ultimate principle in ordinary 'objects' or things. Look for a principle that transcends the subject/object dichotomy rather than treating objects as the ultimate ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle as identity of subject and object (I AM / self-consciousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle manifests itself in the SUM or I AM (spirit, self, and self-consciousness) in which object and subject, being and knowing, are identical; it is a perpetual self-duplication of one power into object and subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground systems in self-consciousness when aiming for an absolute principium cognoscendi. Evaluate claims by whether they account for the identity and reciprocal presupposition of subject and object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-consciousness is an act and implies will/freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Intelligence or self-consciousness is impossible except by and in a will. The self-conscious spirit is a will; freedom must be assumed as a ground of philosophy and can never be deduced from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical accounts of consciousness should treat self-awareness as active and volitional. If a theory omits will or freedom as fundamental, note this as a potential defect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendental method: seek the last in our knowing within knowing
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcendental philosopher does not inquire into an ultimate ground out of our knowing, but what is the last in our knowing itself, beyond which we cannot pass. The principle of our knowing is sought within the sphere of our knowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a methodological rule, examine phenomena from within the capacities of knowledge rather than positing inaccessible external grounds. Evaluate systems by their internal closure and reflexivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid infinite regress by positing an absolute identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempting to explain everything by prior grounds leads to infinite regressus; to avoid this either break arbitrarily or affirm an absolute something that is causa sui and the identity of subject and object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess explanatory chains for regress; prefer accounts that terminate coherently in a principled unity rather than ad hoc stops or endless grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use technical terms when they reduce confusion and aid memory
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical terms in philosophy are justified when they preclude confusion of thought and assist the memory by the exclusive singleness of their meaning more than they bewilder by strangeness (examples: 'multeity' vs 'multitude', 'potence', 'potenziate').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer precise terminology that clarifies kind (abstracting degree) or avoids long circumlocutions. Introduce neologisms sparingly and justify them by their explanatory utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer precision over picturable representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The modern creed that nothing is a clear conception unless representable by a distinct image reduces the conceivable to the picturable; this is a mistaken restriction on clear thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not discard abstract, non-picturable concepts simply because they lack direct sensory imagery. Value conceptual precision even if it resists immediate visualization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and address different audience prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Different judges bring varied prejudices: practical men who desire immediate utility, those alarmed by prior metaphysical abuses (religious/moral prejudices), and those attached to established nomenclature. Responses include appeals to venerable authorities, demonstrating practical value, and showing necessity for new terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing or defending philosophy, tailor arguments to audience classes: show utility to practical readers, defend religiously sensitive readers by clarifying distinctions, and justify terminological innovations to trained metaphysicians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconcile reason with common sense and elevate common sense into reason
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the two-fold function of philosophy to reconcile reason with common sense, and to elevate common sense into reason. True realism is the immediate faith in the object presented (the table itself), not an abstract hypothetical explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid philosophical systems that alienate common human intuitions; strive to connect systematic thought to ordinary experience so that philosophy both respects and refines common sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject vague, indefinite nomenclature that conceals error
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors in metaphysical schools often hide behind plausible and indefinite nomenclature; the attempt is to demonstrate the vagueness or insufficiency of such terms which conceal error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique theories that rely on slippery, undefined terms. Demand explicit definitions and show how vague language can mask conceptual failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insist on systematic unity and logical connection; avoid aphoristic eclecticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Popular aphorisming eclectics dismiss system and logical connection, picking whatever is most plausible and showy. This 'corruption' leads to loss of taste and faculty for system and philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value systematic exposition and clear logical links between propositions; treat isolated aphorisms or fashionable miscellany as an anti-pattern in philosophical writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate imagination and fancy by distinct functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The imagination (shaping and modifying power) is distinct from the fancy (aggregative and associative power). Aggregative/associative operations belong to the Fancy, not properly to the Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing poetic or mental faculties, assign operations to specific faculties. Do not conflate evocative combinatory operations (fancy) with the generative, shaping power attributed to imagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ mathematical analogy and formal schemes in metaphysical construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The mathematician's positions (e.g., negative quantities, rigor of geometry) may furnish materials or hints for metaphysical investigation; apply mathematical method 'mutatis mutandis' to philosophical subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analogies to rigorous sciences to structure metaphysical arguments, borrowing formal distinctions (such as opposites that neutralize vs opposites that produce a new result) to clarify metaphysical dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model intelligence as interacting counteracting forces that generate finitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce intelligence to a kind with two opposite, indestructible forces (centrifugal and centripetal). Their counteraction (not mere opposite directions) produces a tertium aliquid — a finite generation or interpenetration partaking of both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct explanatory models that generate observable phenomena (e.g., minds, perceptions) as outcomes of interacting principles rather than as brute givens. Evaluate models by their capacity to produce intermediate results rather than nullification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh neologisms against vagueness: neologisms are permissible if they improve clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual and new-coined words are doubtless an evil; but vagueness, confusion, and imperfect conveyance of thoughts are far greater. New terms are legitimate when no adequate existing term exists and when the privilege accords with the end of clear thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce new vocabulary only when it solves ambiguity or avoids long circumlocutions; be ready to justify choices and demonstrate correspondence to intended concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of public reception when placing abstruse chapters in works for general readers
rubrics_metrics.description: A friend advises withdrawing abstruse philosophical chapters from works aimed at a general poetry-reading public and reserving them for specialized treatises; public may be bewildered by dense metaphysical exposition appended to poetic volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider audience expectations and the framing of a work: place highly technical or speculative material in venues/readers expect, or provide appropriate signposting and explanatory framing when including it in broader publications.
